questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The language. I wanted to improve my French.
I was curious about how university studies are in France
The reputation of Sorbonne
That Paris has a lot of Art museums, and Sorbonne a big department of Art History, with a lot of interesting classes.
It gave me the opportunity to study 'Cinema'

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The bureaucracy was a nightmare.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Very hard
I think it was very confusing, with no clear answers or procedures. It was impossible to sign up for classes and complete the Learning Agreement until the semester already started. For me, the learning agreement was not completed until a month after my arrival. 
This was very stressing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Very little. Nobody really helped, and nobody could tell who to ask. 
This was very badly organised

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: As i have some handicaps, i got a studio in a Crous facility. I think i was very lucky.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's nice to have a monthly Metro card.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This process was awful. There was no course descriptions available, and no course numbers until the last minute.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Just days before the semester start, the list of corurses was available. Everything is written in French.
Then there were two different places to sign in. One for the course and the a 'pedagogical sign in... I don't know how it was supposed to be done. Everybody i asked could not help. There was a lot of different webpages where i had to log in and do things... i never got there. At last i desperately went to one of the offices again, crying, begging them to just do the sign-in for me. And so they finally helped me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: When the sign-in finally was done, it was all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you go to Sorbonne, then you must accept that it's a mess, and you have to be patient

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I liked the experience of a very different way of having classes. 
The exams was very old fashionned, with paper and pen and no notes or any other help. This was very difficult as a non native French speaker. It was allowed to have a paper dictionary, but that was a poor help for a written assignment.
The classes were super interesting

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think they were well defined and it was easy to see the purpose of each one.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At Sorbonne, it was mostly the teacher speaking and the students taking notes. No group work or class discussions. It was very focused, and the teachers very professional and efficient.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Iconographie Religieuse
Premier Renaissance Italy
Grande Questions de l'histoire de l'art
Naissance du Cinema
Mise en scene
Economie du cinema

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All of them were fabulous.
Iconographie Religieuse was extremely relevant for all about Art History. I really found this class fantastic. The teacher is great and you get 6 ects for only 1,5 hours per week.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use any, but i think there were lot's of opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not sure

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to Museums.
Go for walks in all the beautiful parks. 
Sometimes, don't take public transport, but just walk the city for several hours.
Join meet up groups/ expat groups on Facebook, to meet other people to ask for advise.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
I think it was a bit hard to make French friends. I mainly connected with other exchange students.
But, everybody was open to help and ask questions, and also to share their notes from the classes with me.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I don't know

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The exams with pen and paper

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The way of teaching at the University.
The coffee, and cafés everywhere. Lots of book shops. People are in generel more interested in litterature, arts, theaters, small cinemas etc. Lot's of fine culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be patient. Everything will sort itself out, one way or the other. Ask, ask, ask. You have to be a bit pushy to get things done.
Ask co-students to share their notes with you in all classes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think i already answered that

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The content of the classes
Getting to know Paris and all its museums.
As art historian, i expanded my knowledge a lot
My French got a lot better
I now have a lot of friends and contacts in Paris

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The lack of systematic help and information
A lot of information was in French only

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
